key_insight: DEEPRUBRIC improves reinforcement learning for deep research agents by supervising rewards with an evidence tree, making rubric-based training more reliable and efficient. Instead of relying only on a query-generated rubric, it grounds evaluation in the underlying evidence structure needed for a strong report.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the inefficiency of rubric-based reinforcement learning for long-form research agents when rubrics fail to capture the full information scope and evidence requirements of a task. This can lead to weak reward signals and poor optimization.
method: Build an evidence-tree rubric that organizes supporting evidence into a structured supervision signal.
Use this rubric to define checkable criteria for reinforcement learning of deep research agents.
Improve alignment between query intent, evidence coverage, and report quality during training.
impact: This matters because it can make training deep research agents more sample-efficient and more faithful to evidence, improving the quality of generated long-form reports. Practitioners get a more reliable way to optimize agents on tasks where correctness depends on comprehensive sourcing and reasoning.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: query -> retrieved evidence -> evidence tree -> rubric reward -> final report
Side-by-side comparison of standard query-generated rubric vs evidence-tree rubric
Tree visualization showing evidence branches supporting different claims
Reward signal chart illustrating improved training efficiency and coverage
paper_title: DEEPRUBRIC: Evidence-Tree Rubric Supervision for Efficient Reinforcement Learning of Deep Research Agents
paper_authors: Minghang Zhu, Chuyang Wei, Junhao Xu, Yilin Cheng, Zhumin Chen
